month|2026-08|site|M11.t:
Leicester went from a good month to a bad one. 32 reviews at 4.34 against 45 at 4.71, negatives 4.4 per cent to 15.6 per cent, more than double the fleet rate and the second lowest average in the fleet.

The cause reads as cover, not cooking. Six issues are inattentive or forgotten service, four are speed, two are dirty tables. A guest on 25/08/2026 writes "skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow", and a five star reviewer noted one server on the floor at peak.

Inka Cheung and Amy Tang should check the rota against covers first, then agree clearing and check back routines with Caroline and JJ. Watch into September, do not judge one month.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M11.t: Leicester is at 9.1% negative against 5.5%, average 4.56 on 77 reviews, so small numbers but a clear pattern. Protein is the theme: six of the 13 food quality issues, with a hard-boiled ramen egg, burnt pork katsu and shredded pork instead of slices on 24/07/2026, and boiled flavourless chicken on 18/08/2026. Service adds seven issues, six of them inattentive, including two 1-star visits on 03/08/2026 and 04/08/2026 that both name dirty tables and an unavailable ramen. One guest wrote "Skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow". Executive Chef on protein prep; Inka Cheung and Amy Tang on peak cover with Caroline and JJ.

week|2026-08-24|site|M11.t: Leicester averaged 3.20 on 5 reviews, down from 4.62 on 8, with 2 negatives. Small numbers, so this is watch rather than act, but both one stars say the same thing. One reports tasteless ramen, steak overcooked against a medium rare request and an egg that was not runny. The other reports long waits, lukewarm food and a slow bill: "Skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow". Labour hours fell 429.4 to 415.0 on sales close to target, so the speed complaint and the rota point the same way. Caroline and JJ to walk the Friday and Saturday deployment with Inka Cheung and Amy Tang, and Executive Chef to re-check the steak cook.

Excellent sushi restaurant with a lovely atmosphere and brilliant service.

I’m glad there were four vegan/vegetarian sushi rolls available, and 3 vegan startets, especially as many places seem to be phasing these options out.

I would love to see a bit more variety though, such as options with egg, cream cheese, tempura or sweet potato, rather than mainly tofu and avocado variations. Vegetable tempura would be a nice option too, there was only prawn tempura.

The presentation was great and the cocktails/spritzes were interesting. The dessert was good too, with a strong matcha flavour in the brownie.

Only small negatives were the soy sauce and wasabi. Although the soy sauce was in Kikkoman bottles, it did not really taste like Kikkoman. It was strangely lacking saltiness, and the wasabi had no kick at all. I know it is not usually real wasabi, but this was very mild. I also tried the non gluten free soy sauce (not sure why this isn't the default one out on tables), but it didn't taste much different.

Overall, I would recommend it and will definitely be back to try the ramen, noodles and katsu.

It is usually difficult to eat high-quality ramen in the UK. If you want it, you have to drive all the way to get a chance to eat good ramen. But you never expected that this chain of Japanese ramen shops that are all around you would be such a surprise! I heard from a friend last time that I ate their ramen and thought the soup base was good, so we all tried it this time. I can't believe we were overjoyed. Their steak ramen is very good and the soup base is well-done and rich in flavor. The pork bone char siu ramen is definitely up to par. Maybe it's because the founder is from Hong Kong and went to Japan to study. So the overall quality is more Asian, and the taste is not spoiled due to localization. I give it a thumbs up. All in all, it's worth a try. I'll come back here next time when I'm craving for Japanese ramen.
